If the emitter’s carbon capture plant can produce CO at, for example, 35 bar, that 2 would significantly reduce the equipment and energy requirements at T-RICH. Aptamus is aware of one capture project in the Midwest that is planning to produce CO at 35 bar for transportation to a 2 liquefaction hub. If the emitter in the Tampa Bay Region that eventually becomes a T-RICH customer can send their CO out at 35 bar, that will be a benefit to T-RICH and improve the business case. 2 Transporting CO via pipeline in gas form at 15 bar is feasible for relatively short distances such as, for 2 example, a pipeline to transport captured CO to T-RICH from an emitter 20 miles away. For longer 2 transport pipelines, a CO condition in a supercritical phase is generally preferred. 2 Receiving System from Rail and Trucks CO is sourced from local or regional emitters. A continual stream of gaseous CO is assumed to be 2 2 provided via pipeline from major emitters. Other emissions are assumed to be received in liquid CO form 2 via road or rail tankers. Liquid CO is unloaded from rail or road cars at three common unloading stations. 2 Each station is equipped with a loading arm package that includes an LCO unloading arm, a CO vapor 2 2 return arm, and one spare arm capable of either service and can service both rail and road cars. Incoming streams are analyzed and metered. Three unloading stations are provided - each station can service both rail and truck transport. Each station is equipped with a loading arm package that includes a LCO unloading arm, a CO vapor return arm, and 2 2 one spare arm capable of either service. Additionally, there are four loading pumps, of which three are operational and one serves as a spare. Each pump has a capacity of 150 m³/h. The loading stations also feature two metering packages, and each package is equipped with an analyzer to ensure that the incoming CO meets product specification and can be transferred directly to storage without any 2 processing. The estimated unloading time for an LCO truck with a capacity of 30m3 is 1 hour, including hose 2 connection and disconnection and product transfer, but excluding truck movement time. Using all 3 unloading stations could allow 25 trucks or approximately 750m³/day to be processed in daylight hours. This frequent truck movement could cause traffic issues in the region and should be investigated further during later phases of the study. The time required to unload the 12×100m³ rail cars that can be brought onto site with one rail movement is estimated to be 4 hours (1 hour per car including connection / disconnection).
